source.text: חֲז֖וֹן עֹֽבַדְיָ֑ה כֹּֽה־אָמַר֩ אֲדֹנָ֨י יְהוִ֜ה לֶאֱד֗וֹם שְׁמוּעָ֨ה שָׁמַ֜עְנוּ מֵאֵ֤ת יְהוָה֙ וְצִיר֙ בַּגּוֹיִ֣ם שֻׁלָּ֔ח ק֛וּמוּ וְנָק֥וּמָה עָלֶיהָלַמִּלְחָמָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Vision of Obadiah. Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh concerning Edom: A report we have heard from with Yahweh, and an envoy among the nations has been sent: Rise up, and let us rise up against her for battle!

en.L: The vision of Obadiah. \q Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} concerning Edom: We have heard a report from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: \q "Rise up, and let us rise up against her for battle!"
en.B: The vision of Obadiah. \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this about Edom: We have heard news from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; a messenger has been sent among the nations: \q "Rise up! Let us rise up against her in battle!"
en.R: This is the vision that Obadiah saw. \q This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says about Edom: A message has come to us from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. A messenger has been sent to the nations to say, \q "Get up! Let us go and attack Edom!"

es.L: Visión de Abdías. \q Así dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} acerca de Edom: Hemos oído un mensaje de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, y un mensajero ha sido enviado entre las naciones: \q «¡{{plural_you:Levántense|Levantaos}}, y levantémonos contra ella para la batalla!».
es.B: Visión de Abdías. \q El Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} dice esto acerca de Edom: Hemos oído una noticia de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; un mensajero ha sido enviado entre las naciones: \q «¡{{plural_you:Levántense|Levantaos}}! ¡Levantémonos contra ella para la batalla!».
es.R: Esta es la visión que tuvo Abdías. \q Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}} acerca de Edom: Nos ha llegado un mensaje de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. Se ha enviado un mensajero a las naciones para decirles: \q «¡{{plural_you:Levántense|Levantaos}}! ¡Vamos a atacar a Edom!».

fr.L: Vision d’Abdias. \q Ainsi parle le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} au sujet d’Édom : Nous avons entendu une nouvelle de la part {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, et un messager a été envoyé parmi les nations : \q « Levez-vous, et levons-nous contre elle pour le combat ! »
fr.B: Vision d’Abdias. \q Le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} dit ceci au sujet d’Édom : Nous avons appris une nouvelle de la part {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; un messager a été envoyé parmi les nations : \q « Debout ! Levons-nous pour la combattre ! »
fr.R: Voici la vision qu’Abdias a reçue. \q Voici ce que dit le Seigneur {{divine_name:DIEU|Yahvé}} au sujet d’Édom : Nous avons entendu un message de la part {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. Un messager a été envoyé aux nations pour dire : \q « Debout ! Allons attaquer Édom ! »

sw.L: Maono ya Obadia. \q Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} asema hivi kuhusu Edomu: Tumesikia habari kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, na mjumbe ametumwa kati ya mataifa: \q "Inukeni, na tuinuke juu yake kwa vita!"
sw.B: Maono ya Obadia. \q Hivi ndivyo Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} asemavyo kuhusu Edomu: Tumesikia habari kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; mjumbe ametumwa kati ya mataifa: \q "Inukeni! Na tuinuke tupigane naye vita!"
sw.R: Haya ndiyo maono aliyoyaona Obadia. \q Hili ndilo Bwana {{divine_name:MUNGU|Yahwe}} analosema kuhusu Edomu: Tumepata ujumbe kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Mjumbe ametumwa kwa mataifa kusema, \q "Amkeni! Twendeni tukaishambulie Edomu!"

ko.L: 오바댜의 환상. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 에돔에 관하여 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 우리가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 소식을 들었다. 사신이 민족들 가운데 보내졌다. \q "일어나라, 우리가 일어나 그를 치러 싸우러 가자!"
ko.B: 오바댜의 환상이다. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 에돔에 관하여 이렇게 말씀하신다. 우리가 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 소식을 들었다. 사신이 민족들에게 보내졌다. \q "일어나라! 일어나 그를 치러 전쟁에 나가자!"
ko.R: 이것은 오바댜가 본 환상이다. \q 주 {{divine_name:하나님|야훼}}께서 에돔에 관하여 하시는 말씀이다. 우리는 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 주신 소식을 들었다. 사신이 민족들에게 보내져서 이렇게 말한다. \q "일어나라! 가서 에돔을 공격하자!"

vi.L: Khải tượng của Áp-đia. \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này về Ê-đôm: Chúng tôi đã nghe một tin từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và một sứ giả đã được sai đến giữa các dân tộc: \q "Hãy đứng dậy, chúng ta hãy đứng dậy ra trận đánh nó!"
vi.B: Khải tượng của Áp-đia. \q Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy về Ê-đôm: Chúng tôi đã nghe tin từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; một sứ giả đã được sai đến giữa các dân tộc: \q "Hãy đứng dậy! Chúng ta hãy đứng dậy ra trận đánh nó!"
vi.R: Đây là khải tượng Áp-đia đã thấy. \q Đây là lời Chúa là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán về Ê-đôm: Chúng tôi đã nhận được một sứ điệp từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. Một sứ giả đã được sai đến các dân tộc để nói: \q "Hãy đứng dậy! Chúng ta hãy đi tấn công Ê-đôm!"

pt.L: A visão de Obadias. \q Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} a respeito de Edom: Ouvimos uma notícia da parte {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}, e um mensageiro foi enviado entre as nações: \q "Levantem-se, e levantemo-nos contra ela para a batalha!"
pt.B: A visão de Obadias. \q Assim diz o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} sobre Edom: Ouvimos uma notícia da parte {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; um mensageiro foi enviado entre as nações: \q "Levantem-se! Vamos nos levantar contra ela para a batalha!"
pt.R: Esta é a visão que Obadias teve. \q É isto que o Senhor {{divine_name:DEUS|Javé}} diz sobre Edom: Ouvimos uma mensagem da parte {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. Um mensageiro foi enviado às nações para dizer: \q "Levantem-se! Vamos atacar Edom!"

decisions.choice: the vision of Obadiah: the title of the book, naming the prophet and what he received
decisions.reason: "Vision" is the word that heads Isaiah (1:1) and Nahum (1:1): a message the prophet received from God, not only a sight he saw. The name Obadiah means "servant of the LORD" and was common (1 Kings 18:3; Ezra 8:9). Nothing else is known of this prophet, and the book gives no date. Verses 11-14 describe Edom standing by when foreigners entered Jerusalem; this is usually taken to be the fall of the city to Babylon in 586 BC (Psalm 137:7; Lamentations 4:21-22), which would place the book soon after it. The book does not say so itself.

decisions.choice: verses 1-9 share much of their wording with Jeremiah 49:9-16; this verse is Jeremiah 49:14
decisions.reason: The same report, the envoy sent among the nations and the call to battle against Edom stand in Jeremiah's oracle on Edom (49:14). The wording is reused here where the Hebrew is the same. The differences: Jeremiah says "I have heard", Obadiah "we have heard", joining the prophet with the people who hear the news; and the envoy's call is shorter here, "Rise up, and let us rise up against her", where Jeremiah has "Gather together and come against her, and rise up for battle". Which prophet drew on the other, or whether both drew on an older oracle, cannot be known.

decisions.choice: the envoy's words: the nations call one another to war against Edom
decisions.reason: The envoy is a messenger sent by the LORD among the nations. The words in quotation marks are his summons, and "let us rise up" makes the nations speak with one voice. "Her" is Edom, spoken of as a woman, as lands and cities often are in the prophets. So the LORD is gathering the nations against Edom, though they do not know it.

decisions.choice: Thus says the Lord GOD (L); The Lord GOD says this (B); This is what the Lord GOD says (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set for the prophets, with the divine name after "Lord" as "the Lord GOD". Literal and Balanced reuse the wording of Jeremiah 49:14 for the rest of the verse; Balanced keeps "Rise up" twice, as the Hebrew does. Readable keeps Jeremiah's "A messenger has been sent to the nations to say", names Edom for "her", and turns "for battle" into "attack". The envoy's call takes double quotation marks as speech quoted inside the oracle.

decisions.choice: the Spanish of Jeremiah 49:14 ("un mensaje de parte del SEÑOR", "un mensajero ha sido enviado entre las naciones")
decisions.reason: Obadiah 1-9 reuses the Spanish of Jeremiah 49:9-16 wherever the Hebrew is the same, as the terms note sets; here Obadiah has "we have heard" and "let us rise up", where Jeremiah has "I have heard" and "come against her".

decisions.choice: "Abdías"
decisions.reason: The prophet's published Spanish name.

decisions.choice: "Abdias"; verses 1-9 reuse the published French Jeremiah 49:9-16 at each level where the Hebrew is the same ("une nouvelle de la part du SEIGNEUR", "un messager a été envoyé parmi les nations"), changing only what Obadiah changes ("Nous avons entendu", "levons-nous contre elle")
decisions.reason: The usual French name of the prophet; and the term sheet asks that the parallel passage read as the published Jeremiah does, so the reader can see the two prophets share these lines.

decisions.choice: Obadiah's oracle is speech: present, future, passé composé and imparfait at every level, never passé simple
alternatives: passé simple for Edom's past deeds
decisions.reason: As the other prophets in French; the account of what Edom did on Jerusalem's day of disaster (verses 11-14) is part of the spoken accusation.

decisions.choice: "habari kutoka kwa BWANA", "mjumbe ametumwa kati ya mataifa" (L, B) as Jeremiah 49:14
decisions.reason: Obadiah 1-9 shares its wording with Jeremiah 49:9-16, so each level reuses the published Swahili of Jeremiah where the Hebrew is the same. Here the Hebrew differs: "we have heard" (Jeremiah "I") and the call "Rise up, and let us rise up against her".

decisions.choice: "Bwana MUNGU asema hivi" (L); "Hivi ndivyo Bwana MUNGU asemavyo" (B); "Hili ndilo Bwana MUNGU analosema" (R)
decisions.reason: The messenger formula with the Lord GOD, as in Amos; "Obadia" as the name is published elsewhere.

decisions.choice: Verses 1–9 reuse the Korean Jeremiah 49:9–16 where the Hebrew is the same: "{{divine_name:주|야훼}}께로부터 소식을 들었다. 사신이 민족들 가운데 보내졌다" (Jeremiah 49:14), changing only what Obadiah changes ("우리가" for Jeremiah's "내가"; "일어나 … 싸우러 가자")
decisions.reason: The term sheet's rule for parallel passages; Edom as a woman is "그" (L, B) or named (R), never "그녀".

decisions.choice: "오바댜의 환상" (L, B); "오바댜가 본 환상" (R)
decisions.reason: The book's title with the Protestant spelling of the prophet's name.

decisions.choice: the wording of the published Jeremiah 49:14 at each level ("một tin từ CHÚA", "một sứ giả đã được sai đến giữa các dân tộc"), with "Chúng tôi" for Obadiah's "we"
decisions.reason: Obadiah 1-9 shares its Hebrew with Jeremiah 49:9-16, so each level reuses the Jeremiah Vietnamese and changes only what the Hebrew changes: here "we have heard" where Jeremiah has "I have heard".

decisions.choice: "Khải tượng của Áp-đia" (L, B); "Đây là khải tượng Áp-đia đã thấy" (R)
decisions.reason: The book title, with the published name Áp-đia. "Chúa là CHÚA" for the Lord GOD and "ngươi" for Edom in rebuke follow the terms sheet, as in Amos.

decisions.choice: A visão de Obadias (L, B); Esta é a visão que Obadias teve (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the title keeps the noun "visão" (m1) at Literal and Balanced, as the Portuguese of Isaiah 1:1 does, and Readable makes it a sentence, as the English Readable does. "Obadias" is the form the Portuguese of 1 Kings 18 and the Chronicles gives the name.

decisions.choice: the Portuguese of Jeremiah 49:14 at each level, with "Ouvimos"
decisions.reason: The report and the envoy repeat Jeremiah 49:14 (m2), so each level keeps that verse's Portuguese ("Ouvi uma notícia da parte do SENHOR ... um mensageiro foi enviado entre as nações"; Readable "uma mensagem ... às nações para dizer"), changing only what the Hebrew changes: "Ouvimos" for Obadiah's "we have heard", and the call "Levantem-se, e levantemo-nos contra ela para a batalha" where Jeremiah has "Reúnam-se e venham contra ela". The formula of the prophets, "Assim diz o Senhor DEUS" (L, B) and "É isto que o Senhor DEUS diz" (R), is as Ezekiel 25 has it.

source.text: הִנֵּ֥ה קָטֹ֛ן נְתַתִּ֖יךָ בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם בָּז֥וּי אַתָּ֖ה מְאֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, small I have made you among the nations; despised [are] you exceedingly.

en.L: Look, I have made you small among the nations; \q you are utterly despised.
en.B: See, I will make you small among the nations; \q you will be utterly despised.
en.R: I will make you weak and unimportant among the nations. \q Everyone will look down on you with scorn.

es.L: He aquí, te he hecho pequeño entre las naciones; \q eres sumamente despreciado.
es.B: Mira, te haré pequeño entre las naciones; \q serás muy despreciado.
es.R: Te haré débil y sin importancia entre las naciones. \q Todos te mirarán con desprecio.

fr.L: Voici, je t’ai rendu petit parmi les nations ; \q tu es extrêmement méprisé.
fr.B: Je te rendrai petit parmi les nations ; \q tu seras profondément méprisé.
fr.R: Je ferai de toi un peuple faible et sans importance parmi les nations. \q Tout le monde te regardera avec mépris.

sw.L: Tazama, nimekufanya mdogo kati ya mataifa; \q umedharauliwa mno.
sw.B: Tazama, nitakufanya mdogo kati ya mataifa; \q utadharauliwa mno.
sw.R: Nitakufanya dhaifu na usiye na maana kati ya mataifa. \q Kila mtu atakudharau.

ko.L: 보라, 내가 너를 민족들 가운데서 작게 만들었다. \q 너는 몹시 멸시를 받는다.
ko.B: 보라, 내가 너를 민족들 가운데서 보잘것없게 만들겠다. \q 너는 몹시 멸시를 받을 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 너를 민족들 가운데서 약하고 하찮은 나라로 만들겠다. \q 모든 사람이 너를 업신여길 것이다.

vi.L: Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã làm cho ngươi nhỏ bé giữa các dân tộc; \q ngươi bị khinh bỉ vô cùng.
vi.B: Này, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ làm cho ngươi nhỏ bé giữa các dân tộc; \q ngươi sẽ bị mọi người khinh bỉ vô cùng.
vi.R: Ta sẽ làm cho ngươi yếu ớt và tầm thường giữa các dân tộc. \q Mọi người sẽ khinh dể ngươi.

pt.L: Eis que te fiz pequeno entre as nações; \q tu és muito desprezado.
pt.B: Vê: farei de ti uma nação pequena entre as nações; \q serás desprezado ao extremo.
pt.R: Vou te deixar fraco e sem importância entre as nações. \q Todos vão te olhar com o maior desprezo.

decisions.choice: small among the nations, despised: as Jeremiah 49:15
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 49:15 has the same first line. Its second line reads "despised among humankind"; here it is "you are utterly despised". Jeremiah's verse also begins with "for", which Obadiah lacks.

decisions.choice: I have made you small: the completed form for what God will surely do
alternatives: Edom has already been made small
decisions.reason: The verb has the form used for completed action, but the verses that follow speak of Edom's fall as still to come (verses 4, 8). The prophets often use this form for what God has decided and will surely do, as in Jeremiah 49:15. The same holds for the completed forms in verses 5-7.

decisions.choice: I will make (B, R); utterly despised (L, B); look down on you with scorn (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable reuse the wording of Jeremiah 49:15 and say "I will make" for the completed form (m2). Readable makes "despised" plain and keeps the force of "utterly" with "with scorn".

decisions.choice: the Spanish of Jeremiah 49:15
decisions.reason: Reused at each level; Obadiah's second line "you are utterly despised" differs from Jeremiah's "despised among men", and only that line changes.

decisions.choice: the wording of Jeremiah 49:15 at each level
decisions.reason: Obadiah 2 is Jeremiah 49:15; the Swahili differs only where the Hebrew does ("utterly despised" for "despised among humankind").

decisions.choice: the wording of Jeremiah 49:15 at each level
decisions.reason: Shared with Jeremiah 49:15; Obadiah has "utterly despised" where Jeremiah has "despised among humankind", and only that line changes.

decisions.choice: the Portuguese of Jeremiah 49:15; Vê (B); tu (God to Edom)
decisions.reason: The first line is Jeremiah 49:15 (m1), and each level keeps its Portuguese: "eis que te fiz pequeno entre as nações" (L), "farei de ti uma nação pequena entre as nações" (B), "Vou te deixar fraco e sem importância entre as nações" (R). Obadiah has no "for", so "Pois" goes, and Balanced says "Vê" to Edom rather than Jeremiah's "vejam". For the whole book: God speaks to Edom as one, with "tu", as Jeremiah 49:11-16 does; only verse 16 turns to "vocês", where the Hebrew turns plural.

source.text: זְד֤וֹן לִבְּךָ֙ הִשִּׁיאֶ֔ךָ שֹׁכְנִ֥י בְחַגְוֵי־סֶּ֖לַע מְר֣וֹם שִׁבְתּ֑וֹ אֹמֵ֣ר בְּלִבּ֔וֹ מִ֥י יוֹרִדֵ֖נִי אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] presumption of your heart has deceived you, [you] dwelling in [the] clefts of [the] rock, [the] height his dwelling, saying in his heart, Who will bring me down [to the] ground?

en.L: The arrogance of your heart has deceived you, \q you dweller in the clefts of the rock, [whose] dwelling [is] on the height, \q who say in [your] heart, \q "Who will bring me down to the ground?"
en.B: The pride of your heart has deceived you, \q you who live in the clefts of the rock, whose home is on the heights, \q who say to yourself, \q "Who can bring me down to the ground?"
en.R: Your pride has fooled you. \q You live in hiding places in the rocky cliffs, and your home is high up. \q You say to yourself, \q "No one can bring me down to the ground!"

es.L: La soberbia de tu corazón te ha engañado, \q tú que habitas en las hendiduras de la peña, [cuya] morada [está] en la altura, \q que dices en [tu] corazón: \q «¿Quién me derribará a tierra?».
es.B: El orgullo de tu corazón te ha engañado, \q tú que vives en las grietas de la roca, cuya casa está en las alturas, \q que te dices a ti mismo: \q «¿Quién podrá derribarme a tierra?».
es.R: Tu orgullo te ha engañado. \q Vives escondido en las grietas de los acantilados, y tu casa está en lo alto. \q Te dices a ti mismo: \q «¡Nadie podrá derribarme a tierra!».

fr.L: L’orgueil de ton cœur t’a trompé, \q toi qui habites dans les fentes du rocher, [dont] la demeure [est] sur la hauteur, \q qui dis dans [ton] cœur : \q « Qui me fera descendre à terre ? »
fr.B: L’orgueil de ton cœur t’a trompé, \q toi qui habites dans les fentes du rocher, qui as ta demeure sur les hauteurs, \q qui te dis : \q « Qui pourra me faire descendre à terre ? »
fr.R: Ton orgueil t’a trompé. \q Tu vis caché dans les falaises de rocher, et ta maison est tout en haut. \q Tu te dis : \q « Personne ne pourra me faire descendre à terre ! »

sw.L: Kiburi cha moyo wako kimekudanganya, \q wewe ukaaye katika mapango ya mwamba, makao [yako yako] juu, \q asemaye moyoni [mwako], \q "Ni nani atakayenishusha chini?"
sw.B: Kiburi cha moyo wako kimekudanganya, \q wewe ukaaye katika mapango ya mwamba, mwenye makao yako juu, \q unayejiambia, \q "Ni nani awezaye kunishusha chini?"
sw.R: Kiburi chako kimekudanganya. \q Unaishi mafichoni katika miamba ya milimani, na makao yako yako juu sana. \q Unajiambia, \q "Hakuna awezaye kunishusha chini!"

ko.L: 네 마음의 교만이 너를 속였다. \q 바위틈에 사는 자야, 높은 곳에 [자기] 거처를 둔 자야, \q [네] 마음속으로 말하는 자야. \q "누가 나를 땅으로 끌어내리겠느냐?"
ko.B: 네 마음의 교만이 너를 속였다. \q 바위틈에 살며 높은 곳에 집을 둔 자야, \q 너는 속으로 말한다. \q "누가 나를 땅으로 끌어내릴 수 있겠느냐?"
ko.R: 네 교만이 너를 속였다. \q 너는 바위 절벽 틈에 숨어 살고, 높은 곳에 집을 지었다. \q 너는 속으로 말한다. \q "아무도 나를 땅으로 끌어내리지 못한다!"

vi.L: Sự kiêu ngạo của lòng ngươi đã lừa dối ngươi, \q hỡi kẻ ở trong kẽ đá, [kẻ có] chỗ ở trên nơi cao, \q kẻ nói trong lòng [mình]: \q "Ai sẽ kéo ta xuống đất?"
vi.B: Lòng kiêu ngạo của ngươi đã lừa dối ngươi, \q hỡi kẻ ở trong kẽ đá, có nhà trên nơi cao, \q kẻ tự nhủ: \q "Ai có thể kéo ta xuống đất?"
vi.R: Lòng kiêu ngạo đã lừa dối ngươi. \q Ngươi sống ẩn trong các vách đá, và nhà ngươi ở trên cao. \q Ngươi tự nhủ: \q "Không ai có thể kéo ta xuống đất!"

pt.L: A soberba do teu coração te enganou, \q tu que habitas nas fendas da rocha, [cuja] habitação [está] na altura, \q que dizes no [teu] coração: \q "Quem me fará descer à terra?"
pt.B: O orgulho do teu coração te enganou, \q tu que moras nas fendas da rocha, que tens a tua casa nas alturas, \q que dizes a ti mesmo: \q "Quem pode me fazer descer até o chão?"
pt.R: O teu orgulho te enganou. \q Moras em esconderijos nos penhascos rochosos, e a tua casa fica lá no alto. \q Dizes a ti mesmo: \q "Ninguém consegue me fazer descer até o chão!"

decisions.choice: the pride that deceives, the clefts of the rock: as Jeremiah 49:16
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 49:16 begins "The terror you cause has deceived you, the arrogance of your heart, you who dwell in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill". Obadiah has only the arrogance of the heart, and in place of the height of the hill it has "the height of his dwelling", followed by Edom's boast, which Jeremiah lacks.

decisions.choice: the clefts of the rock: Edom's rocky heights
decisions.reason: Edom was a land of steep red sandstone mountains, cut by gorges, with towns built high among the cliffs, hard for an army to reach. The word for "rock" is also the name of an Edomite stronghold, Sela (2 Kings 14:7), so a reader may hear the name in it. As in Jeremiah 49:16, the word is taken as the rock country itself.

decisions.choice: his dwelling ... in his heart: the poem moves from "you" to "he" and back, still speaking of Edom
decisions.reason: The Hebrew addresses Edom as "you", then says "the height of his dwelling" and "who says in his heart", and then returns to "you" in verse 4. Such shifts of person are common in Hebrew poetry and do not change who is meant. Edom's boast is a question that expects the answer "no one"; verse 4 gives God's answer.

decisions.choice: [whose] dwelling ... in [your] heart (L); your (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words that join the phrases and keeps the change to "his" visible by leaving the pronoun out rather than switching it. Balanced and Readable say "your" throughout, which is what the shift means (m3). Literal and Balanced reuse "has deceived you" and "the clefts of the rock" from Jeremiah 49:16; Readable reuses its "hiding places in the rocky cliffs" and turns the boast into a statement, which is what the question means.

decisions.choice: the Spanish of Jeremiah 49:16 ("la soberbia de tu corazón", "las hendiduras de la peña")
decisions.reason: Reused at each level where the Hebrew is the same; Edom is addressed with masculine tú, as there.

decisions.choice: a soberba do teu coração ... nas fendas da rocha (L); o orgulho do teu coração ... nas fendas da rocha (B); esconderijos nos penhascos rochosos (R)
decisions.reason: These words are Jeremiah 49:16 (m1), and each level keeps that verse's Portuguese ("tu que habitas nas fendas da rocha", "tu que moras nas fendas da rocha", "Moras em esconderijos nos penhascos rochosos"), without its "terror". The rock is "a rocha", not the name "Sela", as the English and Jeremiah 49:16 have it; the meaning note (m2) gives the name a reader may hear in it.

source.text: אִם־תַּגְבִּ֣יהַּ כַּנֶּ֔שֶׁר וְאִם־בֵּ֥ין כּֽוֹכָבִ֖ים שִׂ֣ים קִנֶּ֑ךָ מִשָּׁ֥ם אוֹרִֽידְךָ֖ נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: If you make high like the eagle, and if between [the] stars [is] set your nest, from there I will bring you down, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: Though you make [it] high like the eagle, \q and though your nest is set among the stars, \q from there I will bring you down, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Though you soar as high as the eagle, \q though your nest is placed among the stars, \q I will bring you down from there, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Even if you fly as high as an eagle \q and build your home among the stars, \q I will bring you down from there, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Aunque te remontes como el águila, \q y aunque entre las estrellas esté puesto tu nido, \q de allí te derribaré, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Aunque te eleves tan alto como el águila, \q aunque tu nido esté puesto entre las estrellas, \q de allí te haré caer, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Aunque vueles tan alto como un águila \q y hagas tu casa entre las estrellas, \q de allí te haré caer, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Même si tu [l’]élèves aussi haut que l’aigle, \q et même si ton nid est placé parmi les étoiles, \q de là je te ferai descendre, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Même si tu t’élèves aussi haut que l’aigle, \q même si ton nid est placé parmi les étoiles, \q je t’en ferai descendre, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Même si tu voles aussi haut qu’un aigle \q et que tu bâtis ta maison parmi les étoiles, \q je t’en ferai descendre, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Ingawa unajenga juu kama tai, \q na ingawa kiota chako kimewekwa kati ya nyota, \q nitakushusha kutoka huko, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Ingawa unapaa juu kama tai, \q ingawa kiota chako kimewekwa kati ya nyota, \q nitakushusha kutoka huko, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Hata ukiruka juu kama tai \q na kujenga makao yako kati ya nyota, \q nitakushusha kutoka huko, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

ko.L: 네가 독수리처럼 높이 [올라가고], \q 네 둥지를 별들 사이에 둔다 해도, \q 내가 거기서 너를 끌어내리겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 네가 독수리처럼 높이 날아오르고 \q 네 둥지를 별들 사이에 둔다 해도, \q 내가 거기서 너를 끌어내리겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 네가 독수리처럼 높이 날아올라 \q 별들 사이에 집을 짓는다 해도, \q 나는 거기서 너를 끌어내리겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

vi.L: Dù ngươi bay cao như chim đại bàng, \q và dù tổ ngươi được đặt giữa các ngôi sao, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ kéo ngươi xuống từ đó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Dù ngươi bay vút lên cao như chim đại bàng, \q dù tổ ngươi được đặt giữa các ngôi sao, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ kéo ngươi xuống từ đó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Dù ngươi bay cao như chim đại bàng \q và làm nhà giữa các ngôi sao, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cũng sẽ kéo ngươi xuống từ đó, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

pt.L: Ainda que [o] eleves como a águia, \q e ainda que entre as estrelas esteja posto o teu ninho, \q dali eu te farei descer, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.B: Ainda que subas tão alto como a águia, \q ainda que o teu ninho esteja posto entre as estrelas, \q dali eu te farei descer, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Mesmo que voes tão alto como uma águia \q e construas a tua casa entre as estrelas, \q dali eu te farei descer, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.

decisions.choice: the eagle's nest and "from there I will bring you down": as Jeremiah 49:16
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 49:16 ends "Though you make your nest as high as the eagle, from there I will bring you down, declares the LORD." Obadiah adds a second line, "and though your nest is set among the stars", which raises the boast as high as it can go. God answers Edom's question in verse 3: he will bring Edom down.

decisions.choice: make high ... is set: the first verb has no object stated, the second is passive
alternatives: you set your nest among the stars
decisions.reason: "Make high" stands without an object; "your nest" may belong to both lines, or the first may mean "soar". The second verb is passive, "is set". Some read it as an active form, "you set", without change of sense.

decisions.choice: among the stars: as high as can be imagined
decisions.reason: The picture is of pride that reaches to the heavens, as in Isaiah 14:13-15, where the king of Babylon says he will raise his throne above the stars of God and is brought down to Sheol.

decisions.choice: make [it] high (L); soar (B); fly (R); build your home (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb with its object supplied in brackets. Balanced and Readable say "soar" and "fly" for an eagle making itself high. Readable says "build your home" for "set your nest", as Jeremiah 49:16 does at that level, and reuses that verse's last line.

decisions.choice: "de allí te derribaré" (L); "de allí te haré caer" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The last line of Jeremiah 49:16 in Spanish; Obadiah adds the stars.

decisions.choice: "Ta cũng sẽ kéo ngươi xuống từ đó, CHÚA phán vậy" (L, B); "... CHÚA phán" (R), as Jeremiah 49:16
decisions.reason: The closing line is word for word Jeremiah 49:16 and keeps its Vietnamese; Obadiah adds "among the stars".

decisions.choice: dali eu te farei descer, declara o SENHOR (L, B); diz o SENHOR (R)
decisions.reason: The end of the verse is Jeremiah 49:16 word for word (m1), and keeps its Portuguese at each level. Jeremiah's first line has the nest in it ("Ainda que faças o teu ninho tão alto como a águia"); here the nest moves to the added line, so Literal says "Ainda que [o] eleves como a águia" and Balanced and Readable say "subas" and "voes" for the eagle, as the English does.

source.text: אִם־גַּנָּבִ֤ים בָּאֽוּ־לְךָ֙ אִם־שׁ֣וֹדְדֵי לַ֔יְלָה אֵ֣יךְ נִדְמֵ֔יתָה הֲל֥וֹא יִגְנְב֖וּ דַּיָּ֑ם אִם־בֹּֽצְרִים֙ בָּ֣אוּ לָ֔ךְ הֲל֖וֹא יַשְׁאִ֥ירוּ עֹלֵלֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: If thieves came to you, if destroyers of [the] night, how you are destroyed! Would they not steal their sufficiency? If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave gleanings?

en.L: If thieves came to you, if plunderers by night \q (how you have been destroyed!), \q would they not steal [only] what was enough for them? \q If grape gatherers came to you, \q would they not leave gleanings?
en.B: If thieves came to you, if robbers came by night \q (how you will be destroyed!), \q would they not steal only as much as they wanted? \q If grape pickers came to you, \q would they not leave a few grapes behind?
en.R: When thieves come at night, \q they take only what they want. \q When people pick grapes, \q they leave a few grapes behind. \q But you will be completely destroyed!

es.L: Si ladrones vinieran a ti, si saqueadores de noche \q (¡cómo has sido destruido!), \q ¿no robarían [solo] lo que les bastara? \q Si vendimiadores vinieran a ti, \q ¿no dejarían rebuscos?
es.B: Si vinieran a ti ladrones, si vinieran asaltantes de noche \q (¡cómo serás destruido!), \q ¿no robarían solo lo que quisieran? \q Si vinieran a ti los vendimiadores, \q ¿no dejarían algunas uvas?
es.R: Cuando vienen ladrones de noche, \q solo se llevan lo que quieren. \q Cuando la gente recoge las uvas, \q deja algunas sin recoger. \q ¡Pero tú serás destruido por completo!

fr.L: Si des voleurs venaient chez toi, si des pillards de nuit \q (comme tu as été détruit !), \q ne voleraient-ils pas [seulement] ce qui leur suffit ? \q Si des vendangeurs venaient chez toi, \q ne laisseraient-ils pas des grappillages ?
fr.B: Si des voleurs venaient chez toi, si des brigands venaient de nuit \q (comme tu vas être détruit !), \q ne voleraient-ils pas seulement ce qu’ils veulent ? \q Si des vendangeurs venaient chez toi, \q ne laisseraient-ils pas quelques grappes ?
fr.R: Quand des voleurs viennent la nuit, \q ils ne prennent que ce qu’ils veulent. \q Quand on fait la vendange, \q on laisse quelques grappes. \q Mais toi, tu seras complètement détruit !

sw.L: Kama wezi wangekujia, kama wanyang'anyi wa usiku \q (jinsi ulivyoangamizwa!), \q je, wasingeiba [tu] kiasi cha kuwatosha? \q Kama wachuma zabibu wangekujia, \q je, wasingeacha masazo?
sw.B: Kama wezi wangekujia, kama wanyang'anyi wangekuja usiku \q (jinsi utakavyoangamizwa!), \q je, wasingeiba tu kiasi walichotaka? \q Kama wachuma zabibu wangekujia, \q je, wasingeacha zabibu chache nyuma?
sw.R: Wezi wanapokuja usiku, \q huchukua tu kile wanachotaka. \q Watu wanapochuma zabibu, \q huacha zabibu chache nyuma. \q Lakini wewe utaangamizwa kabisa!

ko.L: 도둑들이 너에게 왔다면, 밤에 약탈하는 자들이 [왔다면] \q (네가 어찌 이렇게 망했느냐!), \q 그들이 자기들에게 필요한 만큼만 훔쳐 가지 않았겠느냐? \q 포도 따는 자들이 너에게 왔다면, \q 그들이 남은 포도를 남겨 두지 않았겠느냐?
ko.B: 도둑들이 너에게 오더라도, 밤에 강도들이 오더라도 \q (네가 어찌 이렇게 망하게 되었느냐!), \q 그들은 자기들이 원하는 만큼만 훔쳐 가지 않겠느냐? \q 포도 따는 사람들이 너에게 오더라도 \q 포도 몇 송이는 남겨 두지 않겠느냐?
ko.R: 도둑들도 밤에 오면 \q 자기들이 원하는 것만 가져간다. \q 사람들은 포도를 딸 때 \q 몇 송이는 남겨 둔다. \q 그러나 너는 완전히 망할 것이다!

vi.L: Nếu kẻ trộm đến với ngươi, nếu kẻ cướp đến ban đêm \q (ngươi đã bị hủy diệt dường nào!), \q chẳng lẽ chúng không chỉ trộm vừa đủ cho chúng thôi sao? \q Nếu những người hái nho đến với ngươi, \q chẳng lẽ họ không để lại vài trái mót sao?
vi.B: Nếu kẻ trộm đến với ngươi, nếu kẻ cướp đến ban đêm \q (ngươi sẽ bị hủy diệt dường nào!), \q chúng chẳng chỉ trộm vừa đủ những gì chúng muốn sao? \q Nếu người hái nho đến với ngươi, \q họ chẳng để lại vài chùm sót sao?
vi.R: Khi kẻ trộm đến ban đêm, \q chúng chỉ lấy những gì chúng muốn. \q Khi người ta hái nho, \q họ để lại vài chùm sót. \q Nhưng ngươi sẽ bị hủy diệt hoàn toàn!

pt.L: Se ladrões viessem a ti, se saqueadores de noite \q (como foste destruído!), \q não roubariam [só] o que lhes bastasse? \q Se vindimadores viessem a ti, \q não deixariam rebuscos?
pt.B: Se ladrões viessem a ti, se viessem assaltantes à noite \q (como serás destruído!), \q não roubariam só o que quisessem? \q Se viessem a ti os que colhem uvas, \q não deixariam algumas uvas para trás?
pt.R: Quando ladrões vêm à noite, \q levam só o que querem. \q Quando as pessoas colhem uvas, \q deixam algumas uvas para trás. \q Mas tu vais ser destruído por completo!

decisions.choice: the thieves and the grape gatherers: words shared with Jeremiah 49:9
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 49:9 has the same two pictures in the other order, grape gatherers first. Obadiah puts the thieves first, adds "plunderers" beside them, and breaks into the comparison with a cry, "how you have been destroyed!" In Jeremiah the thieves "destroy" what is enough for them; here they "steal" it.

decisions.choice: would they not ... ? Questions that expect "yes": even thieves and harvesters leave something, but Edom's destroyers will leave nothing
decisions.reason: A thief takes what he wants and leaves the rest; pickers leave gleanings on the vine. The cry in the middle of the verse gives the point: Edom will not be treated even that well. Its ruin will be complete (verse 6).

decisions.choice: gleanings: the few grapes left on the vine after the harvest
decisions.reason: The law told harvesters to leave what they missed for the poor and the foreigner (Leviticus 19:10; Deuteronomy 24:21). Even a full harvest left something behind, as in Jeremiah 49:9.

decisions.choice: how you have been destroyed (L); how you will be destroyed (B); But you will be completely destroyed! (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the completed form; Balanced says "will be", as in verse 2 (see the note there). The cry interrupts the sentence, so Literal and Balanced put it in parentheses. Readable states the two pictures first, as Jeremiah 49:9 does at that level, and then says the point plainly in a sentence of its own at the end; "completely" draws out what the questions imply (m2).

decisions.choice: the Spanish of Jeremiah 49:9, in Obadiah's order
decisions.reason: The thieves and the grape gatherers keep Jeremiah's Spanish words ("vendimiadores", "rebuscos", "solo lo que quisieran"), with the two halves in Obadiah's order and his cry "how you have been destroyed" added.

decisions.choice: the thieves and the grape gatherers worded as Jeremiah 49:9
decisions.reason: The two pictures are the same as in Jeremiah 49:9 in the other order, with Obadiah's cry "how you have been destroyed!" between them; the Swahili keeps Jeremiah's lines at each level.

decisions.choice: The thieves and the grape gatherers worded as the Korean Jeremiah 49:9, in Obadiah's order (thieves first)
decisions.reason: Shared wording with Jeremiah 49:9; the exclamation in brackets is Obadiah's own.

decisions.choice: the thieves and grape gatherers in the words of Jeremiah 49:9 at each level
decisions.reason: Shared with Jeremiah 49:9 in the reverse order; Obadiah adds the cry "how you have been destroyed!", which Jeremiah lacks.

decisions.choice: the Portuguese of Jeremiah 49:9, in Obadiah's order; roubariam; saqueadores (L), assaltantes (B)
decisions.reason: The two pictures are Jeremiah 49:9 in the other order (m1). Each level keeps Jeremiah's words for them: "vindimadores ... rebuscos" (L), "os que colhem uvas ... algumas uvas para trás" (B), and Readable's two sentences unchanged. Where the Hebrew differs, so does the Portuguese: "roubariam" for Obadiah's "steal" where Jeremiah has "destruiriam", and the added plunderers, "saqueadores" (L) and "assaltantes" (B).

source.text: אֵ֚יךְ נֶחְפְּשׂ֣וּ עֵשָׂ֔ו נִבְע֖וּ מַצְפֻּנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: How they are searched out, Esau! [How] are sought out his hidden treasures!

en.L: How Esau has been searched through, \q his hidden treasures sought out!
en.B: How Esau will be ransacked, \q his hidden treasures hunted down!
en.R: Esau will be robbed of everything! \q Even his hidden treasures will be found and taken!

es.L: ¡Cómo ha sido registrado Esaú, \q rebuscados sus tesoros escondidos!
es.B: ¡Cómo será saqueado Esaú, \q rastreados sus tesoros escondidos!
es.R: ¡A Esaú le robarán todo! \q ¡Hasta sus tesoros escondidos serán hallados y robados!

fr.L: Comme Ésaü a été fouillé, \q [comme] ses trésors cachés ont été recherchés !
fr.B: Comme Ésaü va être mis à sac, \q ses trésors cachés débusqués !
fr.R: Ésaü sera dépouillé de tout ! \q Même ses trésors cachés seront trouvés et emportés !

sw.L: Jinsi Esau alivyopekuliwa, \q hazina zake zilizofichwa zikatafutwa!
sw.B: Jinsi Esau atakavyopekuliwa kabisa, \q hazina zake zilizofichwa zikisakwa!
sw.R: Esau atanyang'anywa kila kitu! \q Hata hazina zake zilizofichwa zitapatikana na kuchukuliwa!

ko.L: 에서가 어찌 이렇게 샅샅이 뒤져지고, \q 그의 숨긴 보물들이 다 찾아내어졌느냐!
ko.B: 에서가 어찌 이렇게 샅샅이 털리고, \q 그의 숨긴 보물들이 다 드러나게 되겠느냐!
ko.R: 에서는 모든 것을 빼앗길 것이다! \q 숨겨 둔 보물까지 다 찾아내어 빼앗길 것이다!

vi.L: Ê-sau đã bị lục soát dường nào, \q các kho báu giấu kín của nó bị lùng ra!
vi.B: Ê-sau sẽ bị cướp sạch dường nào, \q các kho báu giấu kín của nó bị lùng sục!
vi.R: Ê-sau sẽ bị cướp sạch mọi thứ! \q Ngay cả những kho báu giấu kín của nó cũng bị tìm ra và lấy đi!

pt.L: Como foi vasculhado Esaú, \q procurados os seus tesouros escondidos!
pt.B: Como Esaú será saqueado, \q e os seus tesouros escondidos, rastreados!
pt.R: Vão roubar tudo de Esaú! \q Vão achar e levar até os tesouros que ele escondeu!

decisions.choice: Esau: Edom, the people descended from Esau, and Mount Esau, their mountain country
decisions.reason: Esau, Jacob's twin brother, was the ancestor of the Edomites (Genesis 25:24-30; 36:1, 8-9). So the prophets can call the people "Esau", as Jeremiah 49:8-10 does, and Obadiah uses the names Edom, Esau, the house of Esau and Mount Esau for the same people and land. Mount Esau is the mountain country of Seir, south and east of the Dead Sea, which God gave to Esau (Deuteronomy 2:5). The name Esau keeps the story of the two brothers before the reader: the charge in verses 10-14 is that Edom turned on its brother Jacob.

decisions.choice: searched through, his hidden treasures sought out: close to Jeremiah 49:10
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 49:10 says "I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding places". Obadiah uses other verbs, of searching a place thoroughly, and speaks of treasures rather than hiding places. In Jeremiah God acts; here the verbs are passive, and the plunderers of verse 5 do the searching.

decisions.choice: how Esau has been searched: an exclamation, with a plural verb for the people
decisions.reason: "How" opens a cry, as in verse 5. The first verb is plural, because Esau stands for the people of Edom, while "his hidden treasures" treats Esau as one person. The completed form is read as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: searched through ... sought out (L); ransacked ... hunted down (B); robbed of everything ... found and taken (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable choose verbs that make the picture of looters going through every hiding place plain. Every level keeps the name Esau (m1). Balanced and Readable say "will be", as in verse 2.

decisions.choice: "Esaú" at every level
decisions.reason: Edom is called by its ancestor's name, Esau, at every level, as the English does and as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "Ésaü", "la montagne d'Ésaü" kept at every level beside "Édom"
decisions.reason: The book names Edom by its ancestor Esau, Jacob's brother, which is the ground of its charge (verse 10); every level keeps the names, as the English does, and "la montagne d'Ésaü" follows the term sheet.

decisions.choice: "Esau", "mlima wa Esau" at every level
decisions.reason: Obadiah calls Edom by its ancestor's name; every level keeps the names, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "에서" kept at every level for Edom, and "에서의 산" for Mount Esau
decisions.reason: The book names Edom by its ancestor Esau to recall the brotherhood with Jacob (verse 10); every level keeps the name, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Ê-sau" kept at every level, with "núi Ê-sau" in 8, 9, 19, 21
decisions.reason: Obadiah calls Edom "Esau" and "Mount Esau"; every level keeps the names, as the English does, and the meaning decision explains them. Edom is "nó", as a nation.

decisions.choice: Esaú; a casa de Esaú; o monte de Esaú
decisions.reason: For the whole book: the people keep the name "Esaú" at every level (m1), as the English does and as Jeremiah 49:8-10 has it in Portuguese, and "Mount Esau" is "o monte de Esaú", lowercase "monte" as in "o monte Sião".

source.text: עַֽד־הַגְּב֣וּל שִׁלְּח֗וּךָ כֹּ֚ל אַנְשֵׁ֣י בְרִיתֶ֔ךָ הִשִּׁיא֛וּךָ יָכְל֥וּ לְךָ֖ אַנְשֵׁ֣י שְׁלֹמֶ֑ךָ לַחְמְךָ֗ יָשִׂ֤ימוּ מָזוֹר֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יךָ אֵ֥ין תְּבוּנָ֖ה בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: To the border they have sent you, all [the] men of your covenant; they have deceived you, they have prevailed against you, [the] men of your peace; your bread they set [as] a trap under you; there is no understanding in him.

en.L: To the border they have sent you, all the men of your covenant; \q they have deceived you, they have overpowered you, the men of your peace; \q [those who eat] your bread set a trap under you; \q there is no understanding in him.
en.B: All your allies will drive you to the border; \q your friends will deceive you and overpower you; \q those who share your bread will lay a trap for you. \q There is no understanding in Edom.
en.R: All your allies will chase you out to the border. \q Your friends will trick you and defeat you. \q The people who eat at your table will set a trap for you. \q And Edom will not understand.

es.L: Hasta la frontera te han echado todos los hombres de tu pacto; \q te han engañado, han prevalecido contra ti los hombres de tu paz; \q [los que comen] tu pan han puesto una trampa debajo de ti; \q no hay entendimiento en él.
es.B: Todos tus aliados te echarán hasta la frontera; \q tus amigos te engañarán y te vencerán; \q los que comparten tu pan te tenderán una trampa. \q No hay entendimiento en Edom.
es.R: Todos tus aliados te echarán hasta la frontera. \q Tus amigos te engañarán y te derrotarán. \q Los que comen a tu mesa te pondrán una trampa. \q Y Edom no se dará cuenta.

fr.L: Jusqu’à la frontière ils t’ont renvoyé, tous les hommes de ton alliance ; \q ils t’ont trompé, ils ont eu le dessus sur toi, les hommes de ta paix ; \q [ceux qui mangent] ton pain ont mis un piège sous toi ; \q il n’y a pas d’intelligence en lui.
fr.B: Tous tes alliés te repousseront jusqu’à la frontière ; \q tes amis te tromperont et l’emporteront sur toi ; \q ceux qui partagent ton pain te tendront un piège. \q Il n’y a pas d’intelligence en Édom.
fr.R: Tous tes alliés te chasseront jusqu’à la frontière. \q Tes amis te tromperont et te vaincront. \q Ceux qui mangent à ta table te tendront un piège. \q Et Édom ne comprendra rien.

sw.L: Wamekufukuza mpaka mpakani, watu wote wa agano lako; \q wamekudanganya, wamekushinda, watu wa amani yako; \q [wale walao] mkate wako wameweka mtego chini yako; \q hakuna ufahamu ndani yake.
sw.B: Washirika wako wote watakufukuza mpaka mpakani; \q rafiki zako watakudanganya na kukushinda; \q wale wanaokula mkate wako watakutegea mtego. \q Hakuna ufahamu katika Edomu.
sw.R: Washirika wako wote watakufukuza mpaka mpakani. \q Rafiki zako watakudanganya na kukushinda. \q Watu wanaokula mezani pako watakutegea mtego. \q Wala Edomu haitaelewa.

ko.L: 너와 언약을 맺은 모든 사람이 너를 경계까지 내보냈다. \q 너와 평화를 누리던 사람들이 너를 속이고 이겼다. \q [네] 빵을 [먹던 자들이] 네 밑에 덫을 놓았다. \q 그에게는 깨달음이 없다.
ko.B: 너와 동맹을 맺은 모든 나라가 너를 국경까지 쫓아낼 것이다. \q 너의 친구들이 너를 속이고 이길 것이다. \q 너와 함께 빵을 먹던 자들이 너를 잡으려고 덫을 놓을 것이다. \q 에돔에는 깨달음이 없다.
ko.R: 너와 동맹을 맺은 나라들이 모두 너를 국경 밖으로 쫓아낼 것이다. \q 너의 친구들이 너를 속이고 무찌를 것이다. \q 너와 한 식탁에서 먹던 사람들이 너를 잡으려고 덫을 놓을 것이다. \q 그런데도 에돔은 깨닫지 못할 것이다.

vi.L: Chúng đã đuổi ngươi đến tận biên giới, tất cả những kẻ kết ước với ngươi; \q chúng đã lừa dối ngươi, chúng đã thắng ngươi, những kẻ hòa thuận với ngươi; \q [những kẻ ăn] bánh ngươi đã gài bẫy dưới chân ngươi; \q nơi nó chẳng có sự hiểu biết.
vi.B: Mọi đồng minh của ngươi sẽ đuổi ngươi đến tận biên giới; \q bạn bè ngươi sẽ lừa dối và thắng ngươi; \q những kẻ ăn chung bánh với ngươi sẽ gài bẫy ngươi. \q Ê-đôm chẳng có chút hiểu biết.
vi.R: Mọi đồng minh của ngươi sẽ đuổi ngươi ra tận biên giới. \q Bạn bè ngươi sẽ lừa gạt và đánh bại ngươi. \q Những kẻ ăn cùng mâm với ngươi sẽ gài bẫy ngươi. \q Thế mà Ê-đôm chẳng hiểu gì cả.

pt.L: Até a fronteira te mandaram todos os homens da tua aliança; \q enganaram-te, dominaram-te os homens da tua paz; \q [os que comem] o teu pão puseram uma armadilha debaixo de ti; \q não há entendimento nele.
pt.B: Todos os teus aliados te expulsarão até a fronteira; \q os teus amigos te enganarão e te dominarão; \q os que comem do teu pão te armarão uma cilada. \q Não há entendimento em Edom.
pt.R: Todos os teus aliados vão te expulsar até a fronteira. \q Os teus amigos vão te enganar e te vencer. \q As pessoas que comem à tua mesa vão preparar uma armadilha para ti. \q E Edom não vai perceber nada.

decisions.choice: the men of your covenant ... the men of your peace: Edom's allies and friends
decisions.reason: A covenant here is a treaty between nations. "The men of your peace" are those at peace with Edom, its friends (Psalm 41:10; Jeremiah 38:22). The verse does not name them; nearby peoples such as the Arabian tribes are often suggested. The point is that Edom will be betrayed by those it trusted, as it betrayed its brother.

decisions.choice: your bread ... a trap: those who share your bread will set a trap for you
alternatives: they will set your bread as a trap
they will place a wound under you
decisions.reason: The line is hard. It says "your bread they set a trap under you". It is taken here as short for "those who eat your bread", the friends who share Edom's table (Psalm 41:10 speaks of a friend "who ate my bread" turning against the speaker). The word rendered "trap" is rare; it may mean a snare or net, and elsewhere a word spelled the same way means a wound or sore (Hosea 5:13). Some ancient translations differ here; the sense of betrayal by friends is clear either way.

decisions.choice: there is no understanding in him: Edom, famed for its wisdom, does not see what is happening
alternatives: there is no understanding of it (the trap)
decisions.reason: "Him" is Edom (as in verse 3), and the line leads into verse 8, where God removes understanding from Mount Esau. Read the other way, the phrase means that the trap is set without Edom's knowing it. Both readings say that Edom is caught unawares.

decisions.choice: they have sent you ... deceived you ... overpowered you: completed forms for what will surely happen
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, the completed forms describe what God has decided. Edom's own allies will push it out to its borders, perhaps as refugees or as envoys sent away empty-handed.

decisions.choice: [those who eat] your bread (L); those who eat your bread (B); the people who eat at your table (R); Edom (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the words supplied to make the line read (m2); Balanced and Readable state them. Balanced and Readable name Edom for "him" so the reader is not lost, and use "will" for the completed forms (m4). Readable says "chase you out" for "send you to the border".

source.text: הֲל֛וֹא בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֤י חֲכָמִים֙ מֵֽאֱד֔וֹם וּתְבוּנָ֖ה מֵהַ֥ר עֵשָֽׂו׃

records.literal_gloss: Will I not on that day, declaration of Yahweh, destroy [the] wise from Edom and understanding from [the] mountain of Esau?

en.L: Will I not on that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q destroy the wise from Edom, \q and understanding from Mount Esau?
en.B: On that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q will I not destroy the wise from Edom, \q and understanding from Mount Esau?
en.R: On that day, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q I will destroy the wise people of Edom. \q No understanding will be left on Mount Esau.

es.L: ¿No destruiré yo en aquel día, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q a los sabios de Edom, \q y el entendimiento del monte de Esaú?
es.B: Aquel día, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q ¿no destruiré a los sabios de Edom \q y la inteligencia del monte de Esaú?
es.R: Ese día, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}, \q destruiré a los sabios de Edom. \q No quedará inteligencia en el monte de Esaú.

fr.L: Ne ferai-je pas en ce jour-là, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q disparaître les sages d’Édom, \q et l’intelligence de la montagne d’Ésaü ?
fr.B: Ce jour-là, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q ne ferai-je pas disparaître les sages d’Édom, \q et l’intelligence de la montagne d’Ésaü ?
fr.R: Ce jour-là, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, \q je ferai disparaître les sages d’Édom. \q Il ne restera plus d’intelligence sur la montagne d’Ésaü.

sw.L: Je, katika siku ile, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q sitawaangamiza wenye hekima kutoka Edomu, \q na ufahamu kutoka mlima wa Esau?
sw.B: Siku hiyo, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q je, sitawaangamiza wenye hekima kutoka Edomu, \q na ufahamu kutoka mlima wa Esau?
sw.R: Wakati huo, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, \q nitawaangamiza wenye hekima wa Edomu. \q Hakuna ufahamu utakaobaki katika mlima wa Esau.

ko.L: 그날에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다, \q 내가 에돔에서 지혜로운 자들을, \q 에서의 산에서 슬기를 없애지 않겠느냐?
ko.B: 그날에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다, \q 내가 에돔에서 지혜로운 사람들을 없애고 \q 에서의 산에서 슬기를 없애지 않겠느냐?
ko.R: 그날에, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다, \q 나는 에돔의 지혜로운 사람들을 없애겠다. \q 에서의 산에는 슬기가 하나도 남지 않을 것이다.

vi.L: Trong ngày ấy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, \q chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ diệt trừ những người khôn ngoan khỏi Ê-đôm, \q và sự thông sáng khỏi núi Ê-sau sao?
vi.B: Vào ngày ấy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy, \q chẳng phải {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ diệt trừ những người khôn ngoan khỏi Ê-đôm, \q và sự hiểu biết khỏi núi Ê-sau sao?
vi.R: Vào ngày ấy, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán, \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ diệt trừ những người khôn ngoan của Ê-đôm. \q Trên núi Ê-sau sẽ chẳng còn sự hiểu biết nào.

pt.L: Acaso naquele dia, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q não eliminarei de Edom os sábios, \q e do monte de Esaú o entendimento?
pt.B: Naquele dia, declara {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q não farei desaparecer os sábios de Edom \q e o entendimento do monte de Esaú?
pt.R: Naquele dia, diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, \q vou destruir os sábios de Edom. \q Não vai sobrar entendimento no monte de Esaú.

decisions.choice: the wise of Edom: Edom was known for its wisdom
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's oracle on Edom opens "Is there no more wisdom in Teman?" (49:7), and Job's friend Eliphaz, the wisest of them, came from Teman in Edom (Job 2:11). The verse uses Edom's pride in its wisdom against it: the understanding it lacks in verse 7 will be taken away altogether.

decisions.choice: will I not ... ? A question that expects "yes"
decisions.reason: The question is a strong statement: on that day God will certainly do it. "That day" is the day of Edom's judgment, which verse 15 joins to the day of the LORD on all the nations.

decisions.choice: On that day, declares the LORD, will I not ... (B); I will destroy (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced puts "on that day" first, where English expects it. Readable states the question as the promise it is (m2) and makes the second line a sentence of its own.

decisions.choice: "el monte de Esaú"
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets for Obadiah.

decisions.choice: Acaso ... não eliminarei (L); não farei desaparecer (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is "destroy", but "destruir o entendimento" reads oddly in Portuguese; Literal says "eliminar de Edom" and Balanced "fazer desaparecer", which keep the sense of removing something entirely. "Acaso" at Literal marks the question that expects "yes" (m2).

source.text: וְחַתּ֥וּ גִבּוֹרֶ֖יךָ תֵּימָ֑ן לְמַ֧עַן יִכָּֽרֶת־אִ֛ישׁ מֵהַ֥ר עֵשָׂ֖ו מִקָּֽטֶל׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be dismayed your mighty men, Teman, so that will be cut off everyone from [the] mountain of Esau by slaughter.

en.L: And your mighty men will be shattered, Teman, \q so that everyone will be cut off from Mount Esau by slaughter.
en.B: Your warriors will be terrified, Teman, \q so that everyone on Mount Esau will be cut down in the slaughter.
en.R: Your soldiers, Teman, will be terrified, \q and everyone on Mount Esau will be killed.

es.L: Y tus valientes serán quebrantados, oh Temán, \q para que todos sean exterminados del monte de Esaú por la matanza.
es.B: Tus guerreros se llenarán de terror, Temán, \q y todos los del monte de Esaú caerán en la matanza.
es.R: Tus soldados, Temán, estarán aterrados, \q y todos los del monte de Esaú morirán.

fr.L: Et tes guerriers seront brisés, Téman, \q afin que chacun soit retranché de la montagne d’Ésaü par le massacre.
fr.B: Tes guerriers seront terrifiés, Téman, \q et tous seront abattus sur la montagne d’Ésaü dans le massacre.
fr.R: Téman, tes soldats seront terrifiés, \q et tous ceux qui vivent sur la montagne d’Ésaü seront tués.

sw.L: Na mashujaa wako watafadhaika, ee Temani, \q hata kila mtu atakatiliwa mbali kutoka mlima wa Esau kwa mauaji.
sw.B: Mashujaa wako wataogopa sana, ee Temani, \q hata kila mtu katika mlima wa Esau atakatiliwa mbali katika mauaji.
sw.R: Askari wako, ee Temani, wataogopa sana, \q na kila mtu katika mlima wa Esau atauawa.

ko.L: 데만아, 네 용사들이 놀라 넋을 잃을 것이니, \q 에서의 산에서 모든 사람이 살육으로 끊어질 것이다.
ko.B: 데만아, 네 용사들이 두려워 떨 것이고, \q 에서의 산에 있는 사람은 모두 살육을 당해 쓰러질 것이다.
ko.R: 데만아, 네 군인들이 두려워 떨 것이다. \q 에서의 산에 있는 사람은 모두 죽임을 당할 것이다.

vi.L: Và các dũng sĩ của ngươi sẽ kinh hoàng, hỡi Thê-man, \q để mọi người đều bị diệt trừ khỏi núi Ê-sau bởi cuộc tàn sát.
vi.B: Hỡi Thê-man, các chiến sĩ của ngươi sẽ kinh hãi, \q và mọi người trên núi Ê-sau sẽ bị giết trong cuộc tàn sát.
vi.R: Hỡi Thê-man, binh lính của ngươi sẽ kinh hãi, \q và mọi người trên núi Ê-sau sẽ bị giết.

pt.L: E os teus valentes ficarão quebrantados, Temã, \q para que seja eliminado cada um do monte de Esaú pela matança.
pt.B: Os teus guerreiros ficarão apavorados, Temã, \q e todos no monte de Esaú serão abatidos na matança.
pt.R: Os teus soldados, Temã, vão ficar apavorados, \q e todos no monte de Esaú vão ser mortos.

decisions.choice: Teman: one of Edom's chief regions, standing for the whole land
decisions.reason: Teman was a region, and perhaps a town, in the south of Edom, named after a grandson of Esau (Genesis 36:11). As in Jeremiah 49:7 and 20, it stands for Edom as a whole, beside Mount Esau.

decisions.choice: by slaughter: the last words of verse 9
alternatives: the first words of verse 10: "because of the slaughter, because of the violence done to your brother Jacob"
decisions.reason: The verse division and the accents of the Hebrew text place "by slaughter" at the end of verse 9. Some ancient translations, among them the Greek and the Latin, join it to verse 10, so that Edom is judged "because of the slaughter" of its brother. The Hebrew division is followed. This description of the ancient translations is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: dismayed: shattered with terror
decisions.reason: The verb means to be broken, and so to be broken in spirit, terrified (Jeremiah 49:37). The warriors lose their nerve, and the people are left without defense.

decisions.choice: shattered (L); terrified (B, R); cut down ... killed (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of breaking; Balanced and Readable give its sense here, terror. "Everyone" is the Hebrew "each man"; the sense is everyone left on Mount Esau. Readable says "killed" for "cut off by slaughter".

decisions.choice: quebrantados (L); apavorados (B, R); Temã
decisions.reason: "Quebrantado" keeps the picture of breaking at Literal (m3) and is said of people broken in spirit; Balanced and Readable say "apavorados", as the English says "terrified". Teman is "Temã", as Jeremiah 49:7 has it.

source.text: מֵחֲמַ֛ס אָחִ֥יךָ יַעֲקֹ֖ב תְּכַסְּךָ֣ בוּשָׁ֑ה וְנִכְרַ֖תָּ לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Because of [the] violence [to] your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.

en.L: Because of the violence [done to] your brother Jacob, disgrace will cover you, \q and you will be cut off for all time.
en.B: Because of the violence you did to your brother Jacob, \q you will be covered in shame and cut off forever.
en.R: You were cruel to your brother Jacob's people, so you will be covered with shame, \q and you will be destroyed forever.

es.L: Por la violencia [hecha] a tu hermano Jacob, te cubrirá la vergüenza, \q y serás exterminado para siempre.
es.B: Por la violencia que hiciste a tu hermano Jacob, \q quedarás cubierto de vergüenza y serás exterminado para siempre.
es.R: Fuiste cruel con el pueblo de tu hermano Jacob; por eso quedarás cubierto de vergüenza, \q y serás destruido para siempre.

fr.L: À cause de la violence [faite] à ton frère Jacob, la honte te couvrira, \q et tu seras retranché pour toujours.
fr.B: À cause de la violence que tu as faite à ton frère Jacob, \q tu seras couvert de honte et retranché pour toujours.
fr.R: Tu as été cruel envers le peuple de Jacob, ton frère. Alors tu seras couvert de honte, \q et tu seras détruit pour toujours.

sw.L: Kwa sababu ya udhalimu [uliomtendea] ndugu yako Yakobo, aibu itakufunika, \q nawe utakatiliwa mbali milele.
sw.B: Kwa sababu ya ukatili uliomtendea ndugu yako Yakobo, \q utafunikwa na aibu na kukatiliwa mbali milele.
sw.R: Uliwatendea ukatili wazao wa ndugu yako Yakobo, kwa hiyo utafunikwa na aibu, \q nawe utaangamizwa milele.

ko.L: 네 형제 야곱에게 [가한] 폭력 때문에 수치가 너를 덮고, \q 너는 영원히 끊어질 것이다.
ko.B: 네가 네 형제 야곱에게 휘두른 폭력 때문에 \q 너는 수치를 뒤집어쓰고 영원히 끊어질 것이다.
ko.R: 너는 네 형제 야곱의 자손에게 잔인하게 굴었다. 그래서 너는 수치를 당할 것이다. \q 너는 영원히 망할 것이다.

vi.L: Vì sự bạo ngược [đối với] Gia-cốp, anh em ngươi, sự hổ nhục sẽ bao phủ ngươi, \q và ngươi sẽ bị diệt trừ đời đời.
vi.B: Vì sự bạo ngược ngươi đã làm cho Gia-cốp, anh em ngươi, \q ngươi sẽ bị bao phủ trong hổ thẹn và bị diệt trừ mãi mãi.
vi.R: Ngươi đã tàn ác với dân Gia-cốp, là anh em của ngươi, nên ngươi sẽ bị bao phủ trong hổ thẹn, \q và ngươi sẽ bị tiêu diệt mãi mãi.

pt.L: Por causa da violência [feita] ao teu irmão Jacó, a vergonha te cobrirá, \q e serás eliminado para sempre.
pt.B: Por causa da violência que fizeste contra o teu irmão Jacó, \q serás coberto de vergonha e eliminado para sempre.
pt.R: Foste cruel com o povo do teu irmão Jacó, por isso vais ficar coberto de vergonha \q e vais ser destruído para sempre.

decisions.choice: your brother Jacob: the charge is that Edom wronged its own brother
decisions.reason: Esau and Jacob were twins (Genesis 25:24-26), and the law reminded Israel that "the Edomite is your brother" (Deuteronomy 23:8; compare Numbers 20:14). Edom's guilt is the greater because the violence was done to its own kin. Here the verses turn from Edom's pride to the reason for its judgment, set out in verses 11-14.

decisions.choice: violence: wrong done by force, cruelty
decisions.reason: The word means violent wrongdoing, the cruelty that breaks the bonds between people (Genesis 6:11; Joel 4:19, where it is again used of Edom's violence against Judah).

decisions.choice: [done to] (L); you did to (B); You were cruel to your brother Jacob's people (R); disgrace (L); shame (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "the violence of your brother", meaning the violence done to him. Literal brackets the words that say so; Balanced and Readable state them. Readable says "Jacob's people" because Jacob here stands for the nation descended from him, and "destroyed" for "cut off". Literal says "disgrace" and "for all time", Balanced and Readable "shame" and "forever"; the words mean the same.

decisions.choice: "Gia-cốp, anh em ngươi"
decisions.reason: Esau was Jacob's brother; Vietnamese "anh em" leaves open who is older, as the Hebrew does.

source.text: בְּיוֹם֙ עֲמָֽדְךָ֣ מִנֶּ֔גֶד בְּי֛וֹם שְׁב֥וֹת זָרִ֖ים חֵיל֑וֹ וְנָכְרִ֞ים בָּ֣אוּ שְׁעָרָ֗יו וְעַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ יַדּ֣וּ גוֹרָ֔ל גַּם־אַתָּ֖ה כְּאַחַ֥ד מֵהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: On [the] day you stood aloof, on [the] day strangers carried off his wealth, and foreigners entered his gates, and for Jerusalem they cast lots, also you [were] like one of them.

en.L: On the day you stood aloof, \q on the day strangers carried off his wealth, \q and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, \q you too [were] like one of them.
en.B: On the day you stood at a distance, \q on the day strangers carried off his wealth \q and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, \q you were like one of them.
en.R: You stood by and watched \q when strangers carried off your brother's wealth. \q Foreigners came through his gates and threw lots to divide up Jerusalem. \q You were just like them!

es.L: El día en que te mantuviste aparte, \q el día en que los extraños se llevaron su riqueza, \q y los extranjeros entraron por sus puertas y echaron suertes sobre Jerusalén, \q también tú [eras] como uno de ellos.
es.B: El día en que te quedaste a distancia, \q el día en que los extraños se llevaron su riqueza \q y los extranjeros entraron por sus puertas y echaron suertes sobre Jerusalén, \q tú eras como uno de ellos.
es.R: Te quedaste mirando \q cuando los extraños se llevaron las riquezas de tu hermano. \q Los extranjeros entraron por sus puertas y echaron suertes para repartirse Jerusalén. \q ¡Tú fuiste igual que ellos!

fr.L: Le jour où tu te tenais à l’écart, \q le jour où des étrangers emportaient ses richesses, \q et où des étrangers entraient par ses portes et tiraient au sort Jérusalem, \q toi aussi, tu [étais] comme l’un d’eux.
fr.B: Le jour où tu te tenais à distance, \q le jour où des étrangers emportaient ses richesses \q et où des étrangers entraient par ses portes et tiraient au sort Jérusalem, \q tu étais comme l’un d’eux.
fr.R: Tu es resté là à regarder \q quand des étrangers ont emporté les richesses de ton frère. \q Des étrangers ont franchi ses portes et ont tiré au sort pour se partager Jérusalem. \q Tu étais exactement comme eux !

sw.L: Siku ile uliposimama mbali, \q siku ile wageni walipochukua mali yake, \q na watu wa kigeni walipoingia malango yake na kupiga kura juu ya Yerusalemu, \q wewe pia [ulikuwa] kama mmoja wao.
sw.B: Siku ile uliposimama mbali, \q siku ile wageni walipochukua mali yake \q na watu wa kigeni walipoingia malango yake na kupiga kura juu ya Yerusalemu, \q wewe ulikuwa kama mmoja wao.
sw.R: Ulisimama ukitazama tu \q wageni walipochukua mali ya ndugu yako. \q Watu wa kigeni waliingia kupitia malango yake na kupiga kura ili kuigawana Yerusalemu. \q Wewe ulikuwa kama wao kabisa!

ko.L: 네가 멀리 떨어져 서 있던 날, \q 낯선 자들이 그의 재물을 빼앗아 가던 날, \q 이방인들이 그의 성문으로 들어와 예루살렘을 두고 제비를 뽑던 날, \q 너도 그들 가운데 하나와 같았다.
ko.B: 네가 멀찍이 서 있던 날, \q 낯선 자들이 그의 재물을 빼앗아 가던 날, \q 이방인들이 그의 성문으로 들어와 예루살렘을 두고 제비를 뽑던 날에, \q 너도 그들과 똑같았다.
ko.R: 너는 옆에 서서 구경만 했다. \q 낯선 자들이 네 형제의 재물을 빼앗아 갔다. \q 이방인들이 그의 성문으로 들어와 제비를 뽑아 예루살렘을 나누어 가졌다. \q 너도 그들과 다를 것이 없었다!

vi.L: Trong ngày ngươi đứng xa xa, \q trong ngày những kẻ lạ cướp đi của cải nó, \q và những người ngoại bang vào các cổng thành nó và bắt thăm chia Giê-ru-sa-lem, \q chính ngươi cũng [như] một trong bọn chúng.
vi.B: Trong ngày ngươi đứng từ xa, \q trong ngày những kẻ lạ cướp đi của cải nó \q và người ngoại bang tiến vào các cổng thành nó, bắt thăm chia Giê-ru-sa-lem, \q thì ngươi cũng như một trong bọn chúng.
vi.R: Ngươi đã đứng nhìn \q khi những kẻ lạ cướp đi của cải của anh em ngươi. \q Người ngoại bang tiến qua các cổng thành nó và bắt thăm chia nhau Giê-ru-sa-lem. \q Ngươi cũng chẳng khác gì chúng!

pt.L: No dia em que ficaste de longe, \q no dia em que estranhos levaram as suas riquezas, \q e estrangeiros entraram pelas suas portas e lançaram sortes sobre Jerusalém, \q também tu [eras] como um deles.
pt.B: No dia em que ficaste a distância, \q no dia em que estranhos levaram as suas riquezas \q e estrangeiros entraram pelas suas portas e lançaram sortes sobre Jerusalém, \q tu eras como um deles.
pt.R: Tu ficaste parado, só olhando, \q quando estranhos levaram as riquezas do teu irmão. \q Estrangeiros entraram pelas portas dele e tiraram a sorte para dividir Jerusalém. \q Tu foste igual a eles!

decisions.choice: the day strangers entered Jerusalem: the fall of the city, usually taken to be the Babylonian conquest of 586 BC
alternatives: an earlier attack on Jerusalem, such as that of the Philistines and Arabians in the days of Jehoram (2 Chronicles 21:16-17)
decisions.reason: The verse does not name the enemy. Psalm 137:7 remembers the Edomites crying "Tear it down!" on the day Jerusalem fell to Babylon, and Lamentations 4:21-22 and Ezekiel 35:5, 10-15 also accuse Edom over that disaster. That is the usual identification. Jerusalem was attacked more than once, and the description fits other attacks too.

decisions.choice: his wealth: Jacob's goods, or his army
alternatives: his army, carried off into captivity
decisions.reason: The word means strength, and so either wealth or a fighting force. The verb means to take captive. Carrying off goods fits verse 13, where Edom reaches for Jacob's wealth; but the line can also mean that strangers took his army captive.

decisions.choice: cast lots for Jerusalem: divided the city and its people as plunder
decisions.reason: Victors cast lots to share out captured people and goods (Joel 4:3; Nahum 3:10; Psalm 22:19). Edom took no part in the fighting, but by standing by it was like one of the conquerors.

decisions.choice: stood aloof (L); stood at a distance (B); stood by and watched (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says that Edom stood "from opposite", at a distance, as an onlooker who will not help. Readable says what that meant. Readable names "your brother" for "his", so the reader can follow who is meant, and says "threw lots to divide up" for casting lots (m3).

source.text: וְאַל־תֵּ֤רֶא בְיוֹם־אָחִ֨יךָ֙ בְּי֣וֹם נָכְר֔וֹ וְאַל־תִּשְׂמַ֥ח לִבְנֵֽי־יְהוּדָ֖ה בְּי֣וֹם אָבְדָ֑ם וְאַל־תַּגְדֵּ֥ל פִּ֖יךָ בְּי֥וֹם צָרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And do not look on [the] day of your brother, on [the] day of his misfortune; and do not rejoice over [the] sons of Judah on [the] day of their perishing; and do not make big your mouth on [the] day of distress.

en.L: But do not look on the day of your brother, on the day of his misfortune; \q do not rejoice over the {{gender:children|sons}} of Judah on the day of their ruin; \q do not make your mouth big on the day of distress.
en.B: You should not have gloated over your brother's day, the day of his misfortune, \q nor rejoiced over the people of Judah on the day of their ruin, \q nor boasted so loudly on the day of their distress.
en.R: You should not have enjoyed watching your brother on the day his trouble came. \q You should not have been glad when the people of Judah were destroyed. \q You should not have bragged on the day they were in distress.

es.L: Pero no mires el día de tu hermano, el día de su desgracia; \q no te alegres de los hijos de Judá el día de su ruina; \q no agrandes tu boca el día de la angustia.
es.B: No debiste mirar con gusto el día de tu hermano, el día de su desgracia, \q ni alegrarte por la gente de Judá el día de su ruina, \q ni jactarte tanto el día de su angustia.
es.R: No debiste disfrutar viendo a tu hermano el día en que le llegó la desgracia. \q No debiste alegrarte cuando la gente de Judá fue destruida. \q No debiste burlarte de ellos el día en que estaban angustiados.

fr.L: Mais ne regarde pas le jour de ton frère, le jour de son malheur ; \q ne te réjouis pas au sujet des {{gender:enfants|fils}} de Juda le jour de leur ruine ; \q n’ouvre pas une grande bouche le jour de la détresse.
fr.B: Tu n’aurais pas dû contempler avec plaisir le jour de ton frère, le jour de son malheur, \q ni te réjouir au sujet des gens de Juda le jour de leur ruine, \q ni te vanter si fort le jour de leur détresse.
fr.R: Tu n’aurais pas dû prendre plaisir à regarder ton frère le jour où le malheur l’a frappé. \q Tu n’aurais pas dû te réjouir quand les gens de Juda ont été détruits. \q Tu n’aurais pas dû te vanter le jour de leur détresse.

sw.L: Lakini usiitazame siku ya ndugu yako, siku ya msiba wake; \q usifurahie juu ya wana wa Yuda katika siku ya maangamizi yao; \q usikifanye kinywa chako kikubwa katika siku ya dhiki.
sw.B: Hukupaswa kuifurahia siku ya ndugu yako, siku ya msiba wake, \q wala kuwafurahia watu wa Yuda katika siku ya maangamizi yao, \q wala kujigamba sana katika siku ya dhiki yao.
sw.R: Hukupaswa kufurahia kumtazama ndugu yako siku ile taabu ilipompata. \q Hukupaswa kufurahi watu wa Yuda walipoangamizwa. \q Hukupaswa kujisifu siku ile walipokuwa katika dhiki.

ko.L: 네 형제의 날, 그가 불행을 당하던 날을 보며 [즐거워하지] 말아라. \q {{gender:유다 자손|유다의 아들들}}이 망하던 날에 그들을 두고 기뻐하지 말아라. \q 고난의 날에 네 입을 크게 벌리지 말아라.
ko.B: 너는 네 형제가 불행을 당하던 날에 그것을 보고 고소해하지 말았어야 했다. \q 유다 백성이 망하던 날에 그들을 두고 기뻐하지 말았어야 했다. \q 그들이 고난을 당하던 날에 큰소리치지 말았어야 했다.
ko.R: 너는 네 형제에게 재앙이 닥친 날에 그것을 보며 즐거워하지 말았어야 했다. \q 유다 백성이 멸망할 때에 기뻐하지 말았어야 했다. \q 그들이 고난을 당하던 날에 뽐내지 말았어야 했다.

vi.L: Nhưng đừng nhìn ngày của anh em ngươi, ngày nó gặp bất hạnh; \q đừng vui mừng về con cái Giu-đa trong ngày chúng bị diệt vong; \q đừng mở miệng khoác lác trong ngày hoạn nạn.
vi.B: Ngươi không nên hả hê nhìn ngày của anh em mình, là ngày nó gặp bất hạnh, \q cũng không nên vui mừng về dân Giu-đa trong ngày họ bị diệt vong, \q cũng không nên khoác lác ầm ĩ trong ngày họ gặp hoạn nạn.
vi.R: Ngươi không nên vui thích nhìn anh em mình trong ngày nó gặp hoạn nạn. \q Ngươi không nên vui mừng khi dân Giu-đa bị tiêu diệt. \q Ngươi không nên khoe khoang trong ngày họ gặp khốn khó.

pt.L: Mas não olhes para o dia do teu irmão, para o dia do seu infortúnio; \q não te alegres sobre os filhos de Judá no dia da sua ruína; \q não faças grande a tua boca no dia da angústia.
pt.B: Não devias ter olhado com satisfação para o dia do teu irmão, o dia do seu infortúnio, \q nem ter ficado alegre com o povo de Judá no dia da sua ruína, \q nem ter falado com tanta arrogância no dia da sua angústia.
pt.R: Não devias ter gostado de ver o teu irmão no dia em que a desgraça chegou para ele. \q Não devias ter ficado contente quando o povo de Judá foi destruído. \q Não devias ter falado com orgulho no dia em que eles estavam sofrendo.

decisions.choice: do not look ... do not rejoice: commands spoken as if the day were still before Edom, condemning what it did
alternatives: warnings against doing these things in a disaster still to come
decisions.reason: Verses 12-14 are a series of eight commands, "do not ...". Verse 11 has already described the day as past, so the commands are taken as the prophet's vivid way of condemning what Edom did: he puts himself on that day and cries out against each act in turn. Some read them as warnings for the future. Either way, they set out what Edom is judged for.

decisions.choice: look on: gaze with pleasure; make your mouth big: boast, mock
decisions.reason: To "look on" someone's day of trouble is to watch it with satisfaction (Psalm 22:18; Micah 7:10). To "make the mouth big" is to speak proudly and mockingly (Ezekiel 35:13, again of Edom).

decisions.choice: the day: the day of disaster, named again and again
decisions.reason: The word "day" comes ten times in verses 11-14. The repetition fixes the reader on the one day of Judah's ruin, and leads to "the day of the LORD" in verse 15, when the day will turn on Edom.

decisions.choice: do not (L); You should not have (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the form of the commands. Balanced and Readable say what they mean here, a condemnation of past acts (m1), with "You should not have". Balanced says "gloated" and "boasted so loudly" for the idioms (m2); Readable says "enjoyed watching" and "bragged".

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Judá", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already includes women, so the English gender span has no Spanish counterpart.

decisions.choice: "Tu n'aurais pas dû" (B, R); the imperative "ne regarde pas" (L)
decisions.reason: The commands condemn what Edom has already done (the meaning decision); French says it with the conditional past, as the English "You should not have".

decisions.choice: "wana wa Yuda" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "Wana" covers sons and daughters, so the English gender alternative has nothing to change in Swahili; the same holds in verse 20.

decisions.choice: "…하지 말아라" (L); "…하지 말았어야 했다" (B, R) in 12–14
decisions.reason: The Hebrew forbids what Edom has already done; Literal keeps the prohibitions, and Balanced and Readable say the reproach, as the English does. L's gender span follows the English.

decisions.choice: "đừng ..." (L); "Ngươi không nên ..." (B, R), through verse 14
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses commands as if the day were still ahead, condemning what Edom did (meaning decision); Literal keeps the commands, and Balanced and Readable say what Edom should not have done, as the English does. "Con cái Giu-đa" needs no gender span.

decisions.choice: Não devias ter ... nem ter ... (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the English "You should not have", Balanced and Readable state the commands as a condemnation of what Edom did (m1), in verses 12-14. "Devias" is the past of "dever" that Brazilians use for what someone ought to have done, with "tu" for Edom.

decisions.choice: os filhos de Judá, with no gender setting
alternatives: os filhos e as filhas, under the gender setting
decisions.reason: The English Literal puts "sons" under the gender setting; Portuguese "filhos" already includes daughters, so it takes no span, as "os filhos de Israel" in the Pentateuch and here in verse 20. Balanced and Readable say "o povo de Judá", as the English does.

source.text: אַל־תָּב֤וֹא בְשַֽׁעַר־עַמִּי֙ בְּי֣וֹם אֵידָ֔ם אַל־תֵּ֧רֶא גַם־אַתָּ֛ה בְּרָעָת֖וֹ בְּי֣וֹם אֵיד֑וֹ וְאַל־תִּשְׁלַ֥חְנָה בְחֵיל֖וֹ בְּי֥וֹם אֵידֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not enter into [the] gate of my people on [the] day of their disaster; do not look, also you, on his calamity on [the] day of his disaster; and do not stretch out [a hand] on his wealth on [the] day of his disaster.

en.L: Do not enter the gate of my people on the day of their disaster; \q do not look, you too, on his calamity on the day of his disaster; \q and do not stretch out [your hand] against his wealth on the day of his disaster.
en.B: You should not have marched through the gate of my people on the day of their disaster, \q nor gloated, you of all people, over his calamity on the day of his disaster, \q nor seized his wealth on the day of his disaster.
en.R: You should not have marched through the gates of my people's city on the day disaster struck them. \q You, of all people, should not have enjoyed seeing them suffer on the day of their disaster. \q You should not have taken their wealth on the day of their disaster.

es.L: No entres por la puerta de mi pueblo el día de su calamidad; \q no mires, tú también, su mal el día de su calamidad; \q y no extiendas [la mano] sobre su riqueza el día de su calamidad.
es.B: No debiste entrar por la puerta de mi pueblo el día de su calamidad, \q ni mirar con gusto, precisamente tú, su desgracia el día de su calamidad, \q ni apoderarte de su riqueza el día de su calamidad.
es.R: No debiste entrar por las puertas de la ciudad de mi pueblo el día en que les llegó la calamidad. \q Precisamente tú no debiste disfrutar viéndolos sufrir el día de su calamidad. \q No debiste quedarte con sus riquezas el día de su calamidad.

fr.L: N’entre pas par la porte de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple le jour de leur désastre ; \q ne regarde pas, toi aussi, son malheur le jour de son désastre ; \q et ne tends pas [la main] vers ses richesses le jour de son désastre.
fr.B: Tu n’aurais pas dû franchir la porte de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple le jour de son désastre, \q ni contempler, toi justement, son malheur le jour de son désastre, \q ni t’emparer de ses richesses le jour de son désastre.
fr.R: Tu n’aurais pas dû franchir les portes de la ville de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple le jour où le désastre l’a frappé. \q Toi, plus que tout autre, tu n’aurais pas dû prendre plaisir à le voir souffrir le jour de son désastre. \q Tu n’aurais pas dû prendre ses richesses le jour de son désastre.

sw.L: Usiingie katika lango la watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} katika siku ya maafa yao; \q usitazame, wewe pia, taabu yake katika siku ya maafa yake; \q wala usinyooshe [mkono wako] juu ya mali yake katika siku ya maafa yake.
sw.B: Hukupaswa kupita katika lango la watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} katika siku ya maafa yao, \q wala kufurahia, wewe kuliko wote, taabu yake katika siku ya maafa yake, \q wala kunyakua mali yake katika siku ya maafa yake.
sw.R: Hukupaswa kupita katika malango ya mji wa watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} siku maafa yalipowapata. \q Wewe, kuliko wote, hukupaswa kufurahia kuwaona wakiteseka siku ya maafa yao. \q Hukupaswa kuchukua mali yao siku ya maafa yao.

ko.L: 그들이 재난을 당하던 날에 내 백성의 성문으로 들어가지 말아라. \q 그가 재난을 당하던 날에 너까지 그의 고난을 보며 [즐거워하지] 말아라. \q 그가 재난을 당하던 날에 그의 재물에 [손을] 뻗지 말아라.
ko.B: 너는 내 백성이 재난을 당하던 날에 그들의 성문으로 들어가지 말았어야 했다. \q 재난을 당하던 그날에 다른 누구도 아닌 네가 그의 고난을 보며 고소해하지 말았어야 했다. \q 재난을 당하던 그날에 그의 재물을 빼앗지 말았어야 했다.
ko.R: 너는 내 백성에게 재난이 닥친 날에 그들의 성문으로 쳐들어가지 말았어야 했다. \q 다른 누구도 아닌 네가 재난의 날에 그들이 고통당하는 것을 보며 즐거워하지 말았어야 했다. \q 재난의 날에 그들의 재물을 빼앗지 말았어야 했다.

vi.L: Đừng vào cổng thành của dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong ngày tai họa của họ; \q chính ngươi cũng đừng nhìn tai ương của nó trong ngày tai họa của nó; \q và đừng giơ [tay] lấy của cải nó trong ngày tai họa của nó.
vi.B: Ngươi không nên tiến qua cổng thành của dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong ngày tai họa của họ, \q cũng không nên, chính ngươi, hả hê nhìn tai ương của nó trong ngày tai họa của nó, \q cũng không nên cướp lấy của cải nó trong ngày tai họa của nó.
vi.R: Ngươi không nên tiến qua các cổng thành của dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trong ngày tai họa ập đến trên họ. \q Chính ngươi lại càng không nên vui thích nhìn họ chịu khổ trong ngày tai họa của họ. \q Ngươi không nên lấy của cải của họ trong ngày tai họa của họ.

pt.L: Não entres pela porta do meu povo no dia da sua calamidade; \q não olhes, também tu, para a sua desgraça no dia da sua calamidade; \q e não estendas [a mão] contra as suas riquezas no dia da sua calamidade.
pt.B: Não devias ter marchado pela porta do meu povo no dia da sua calamidade, \q nem ter olhado com satisfação, logo tu, para a sua desgraça no dia da sua calamidade, \q nem ter tomado as suas riquezas no dia da sua calamidade.
pt.R: Não devias ter marchado pelas portas da cidade do meu povo no dia em que a calamidade caiu sobre eles. \q Logo tu não devias ter gostado de ver o sofrimento deles no dia da calamidade deles. \q Não devias ter tomado as riquezas deles no dia da calamidade deles.

decisions.choice: the day of his disaster, three times: a play on the name Edom
decisions.reason: The word for disaster in these lines sounds like the name Edom, and it comes three times, at the end of each line. The sound ties Edom's name to Judah's ruin, and the reader is left to hear that Edom's own disaster is coming (verse 15).

decisions.choice: my people: the LORD speaks
decisions.reason: The oracle began "Thus says the Lord GOD" (verse 1), and here the speaker calls Judah "my people". Edom's wrong was done to the LORD's own people.
